Rapid growth

Across the Valley

Buy three neighboring utilities by December 2014. Once the deals close, their customers expect you to keep the lights on too.

Play Across the Valley↗ Your decisions ↓

Choose your difficulty before you start. It’s free to play in your browser.

Location

Your term
20 years

Your starting point

In 2005 you run Champlain Electric, a fictional utility around Burlington, Vermont. The neighbors you can buy come with equipment, debts and contracts to purchase power.

You still have to run the larger network after the acquisition deadline. Upkeep rises, and the limits on purchased power get tighter in 2017 and again in 2020.

Learn how to play

Your decisions

  1. 01

    Read the purchase terms

    Compare each company's debt and contracts alongside its asking price. How much cash will you have left after the deal closes?

  2. 02

    Check the connections

    See how much power each connection can carry before counting on a neighboring plant to cover a shortage.

  3. 03

    Replace the purchased power

    Check how much supply the contracts will still cover in 2017. Allow time to build replacements while you're paying for network upkeep.
